BiblicalUsage: Plerophoria is full assurance, entire confidence. Hebrews 6:11 says to show diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end, and Hebrews 10:22 to draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith. Paul prays the Colossians may reach the full assurance of understanding in Colossians 2:2, and says the gospel came to the Thessalonians in much assurance in 1 Thessalonians 1:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe assurance is not arrogance — it is the confidence of a child who knows his Father's promise. My position is that God means me to be sure, not to spend my life guessing.
